title: First Interview
description:
A job app led to this.

A small office in Mapo-gu. Third floor. No elevator.
The sign reads 'Mirae Industry Technology Co., Ltd.' — nothing comes up when you search for them.

The interviewer was a woman in her early forties. She picked up the résumé, adjusted her glasses, and read slowly.
The AC hummed loudly. A motorcycle passed outside.

'There's a six-year gap here.'

She set the résumé down and looked at {name}.
'What were you doing?'

Can't say 'paying off debt.' Six years, from twenty-seven to thirty-three, covering for a father who co-signed the wrong loan.
How do you put six years into one sentence.

{name}'s palms were sweating.

choices.text: Tell the truth — 'There were family circumstances.'
choices.result_text:
The interviewer looked at {name} for a moment. Didn't probe further.
Something in her eyes — understanding. Or resignation.
'...I see. You seem like someone who works hard.'

Walking down the stairs, {name} thought:
Whether it leads to a job or not — that was the truth.
And that was the only pride {name} had left right now.

choices.text: Gloss over it — 'I was preparing to start a business.'
choices.result_text:
Packaged it plausibly. The interviewer nodded — but wrote something long in her notes.
Like someone writing 'needs verification.'

Walking down the stairs, {name} thought:
One lie calls for another.
And that weight tends to arrive sooner than expected.

title: The Number
description:
Convenience store night shift. 3 AM.

Difficult customers, stacking deliveries, mopping floors. Slapping 'discount' stickers on near-expiry items.
The fluorescent tubes buzzed. Outside: no one.

Pulled out a calculator.
Just over minimum wage. Not even ₩2,000,000 for a full month of work.
₩3,000,000,000 ÷ ₩2,000,000 = 1,500 months = 125 years.

125 years.

{name} stared at the calculator screen. Laughed. Because what else can you do.
Salary alone — mathematically impossible.

Folding delivery boxes, thinking:
There has to be another way. There has to be.

choices.text: Start by saving aggressively — every won counts. [Saver mindset]
choices.result_text:
Big money starts from small money.
{name} finished the shift and kept scanning job apps. Side work, temp work, two jobs.

Seed money. That's the first gate.
The number 125 years kept drifting in front of the eyes.

choices.text: Start studying investing — money has to make money. [Investor mindset]
choices.result_text:
YouTube, books, finance forums.
After the night shift ended, {name} went to the library.

If salary won't work, money has to work instead.
Compound interest. Leverage. Assets. {name} read those words seriously for the first time.

choices.text: Someday, my own business. Start writing down ideas. [Founder mindset]
choices.result_text:
Behind the register, {name} wrote something in a notebook.
Gaps. Demand. Supply. What nobody else was doing.

Ideas alone are nothing yet.
But people who write nothing down never begin.

title: 2 AM
description:
2 AM. The goshiwon room. Can't sleep.

Staring at the ceiling, {name} opened Instagram out of habit. Fingers scrolling the feed.

High school friend Park Minho — 'Finally my own home 🏠 Housing lottery win ㅠㅠ Waited 10 years #allIn #30sHomeowner'
University classmate Lee Suhyeon — Honeymoon photos. Maldives. Turquoise water. A wedding dress.
Department senior Kim Junghoon — Foreign car key flex. BMW 3 Series. 'First day in the company lot 🔑'

Everyone had arrived somewhere.
Only {name} was still at the starting line. No, behind the starting line.

₩650,000 rent. Bank balance. The stain on the goshiwon wall.

The hand holding the phone grew heavy.

choices.text: Delete the app — comparison is poison.
choices.result_text:
Held it down. Deleted it.
Watching someone else's finish line won't move {name}'s starting line.

The screen cleared a little. The mind — just a little.
But that empty space felt like it could be filled with something.

choices.text: Use that feeling as fuel — just you wait.
choices.result_text:
Envy turned to anger.
'Just you wait' is dangerous — it can burn the person who feels it.

But right now this is all there is to run on.
{name} turned off the phone and closed the eyes. Seoul's night wasn't over yet.

choices.text: Just look. Jealous is jealous.
choices.result_text:
Scrolled to the end. Even hit Like.

Decided not to pretend not to be jealous. That's honest too.
But the honesty of that night — ached a little long.

title: Next Door
description:
Goshiwon shared kitchen. 1 AM.

A narrow space with only one fluorescent tube working.
{name} was pouring hot water into a cup ramen when the door opened behind.

The neighbor from next door. They'd crossed paths before — but this was the first time.
'...You're doing ramen too, hyung.'

He spoke first. Hollows under his eyes. The face of someone who sits for a long time.
Looks about twenty-six. The person whose desk was always piled with notebooks.

'Fourth year studying for the civil service exam. This is my last year — I say that every year.'
He gave a half-laugh. A smile that didn't quite reach the eyes.

'What about you, hyung? What do you do?'

choices.text: 'I don't really know yet. Still figuring it out.'
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu nodded.
'That's the most honest answer.'

The two of them ate ramen in silence in the narrow kitchen.
Just knowing there's someone on the other side of this thin wall in the same situation —
tonight was a little less cold.

choices.text: 'I'm going to Gangnam. Within five years.'
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu stopped mid-ramen and looked at {name}.
Expected a laugh. Didn't get one.
'...You mean it, don't you, hyung.'

A short silence. Then, quietly:
'Somehow I feel like you'll actually go.'
That line stayed. Coming from someone who'd been looking at the same wall for four years.

title: Why Gangnam?
description:
A small real estate office in the Sinchon alleys.
Walked in to check studio apartment prices.

A man in his fifties looked at {name} over his glasses.
'A studio? With your budget, the deposit's going to be tight.'

True — nothing to say to that. About to leave when he called.
'Have a coffee before you go. No customers anyway.'

He made instant coffee, then asked:
'Where do you want to live?'
'...Gangnam.'
He didn't smile or sneer. Just looked.
'Why?'

choices.text: 'I... want to show my father. Just once.'
choices.result_text:
The first time that reason had been spoken out loud.
Im Sangchul looked at {name} for a long moment, then nodded.
'That 'why' is solid. Then that's enough.'
'When you're shaken, it'll hold you. Here's my card — stop by sometime.'
For the first time in an unfamiliar city — {name} had someone to know.

choices.text: 'Doesn't everyone want Gangnam if they have the money?'
choices.result_text:
Im Sangchul chuckled.
'Never seen someone who answered that way actually make it.'
'If Gangnam is the goal, you won't get there. Only people who use Gangnam as a means do.'
Didn't know what that meant then. Left with just the business card.

choices.text: Honest — 'Because I refuse to lose. To this city.'
choices.result_text:
Im Sangchul set down his coffee.
'...I said the same thing thirty years ago. Coming up from South Chungcheong Province.'
'That stubbornness got me this far. Two buildings. But I also lost a lot.'
'You — don't lose anything. If you're going, go without losing.'
There was a weight in that.

title: Contact
description:
Spring afternoon. On the way to work.
Pedaling the bike, turning into an alley — a black Mercedes-Benz S-Class-level sedan swung out and clipped the front wheel.

{name} hit the asphalt. Knee scraped. Front wheel bent.

A woman steps out from the driver's seat. Early thirties. Wet long black hair, a cream tailored suit, and a composure that looks more expensive than the car. But right now, she is clearly shaken.

'Oh no — are you okay? I can call insurance—'

{name} stands the bike back up. Checks the wheel. Checks the watch.
12 minutes to the start of the shift.

choices.text: 'I'm fine.' — Just leave.
choices.result_text:
No compensation, no contact. {name} walks.
Doesn't look back.

The woman stays rooted to the spot, watching the figure recede.
— Never seen anyone do that before.

choices.text: Show the bent wheel — 'Just the repair cost, please.'
choices.result_text:
She takes out two ₩50,000 notes from her wallet. No hesitation.
'Is that enough? If not—'
'It's fine.'

{name} pockets the money and walks.
To her, this was probably lunch money.

choices.text: Get angry — 'You need to watch where you're driving.'
choices.result_text:
Words that had been held in came out. She bows her head.
'...I'm really sorry.'

It seemed genuine. Which made it impossible to stay angry.
{name} sighs and walks the bent bike away.
The weight of her gaze lingered.

title: You Again
description:
Convenience store night shift.
Past midnight. The door chime rings.

{name} stops.
It's her. The woman who drove the car that hit the bike.

She recognizes {name} too. Her eyes go wide.
'...Oh? The one from—?'

A bottle of wine in her hand. Clothes that don't belong in this neighborhood.
Why is she here, at this hour, at this store?

choices.text: Pretend not to know her. Ring it up.
choices.result_text:
'₩15,000.'
{name} scans the barcode mechanically.

She looks like she's about to say something. Hands over the card. Bags up. Picks it up.
At the door, one last look back.
'...You work here.'
The door closes. Chime rings.

choices.text: 'The car.' Acknowledge her first.
choices.result_text:
Her face lights up. Relieved.
'You remember me! I felt so bad — I looked around for a while after you left.'
'Nothing to look for.'
'But people don't usually just walk away like that.'
She hesitates a moment, then:
'I'm Han Jiyeon.'
For the first time that day — a name.

title: Let Me Make It Up to You
description:
A few days later. Coming out after the shift — her car is parked in front.

Han Jiyeon steps out. This time she came with a purpose.

'Let me buy you one coffee. If not that, then a meal.
I can't stop thinking about it. You were the one in the wrong spot, and you left without taking anything.'

Seems genuine. But {name} knows.
They come from different worlds. A cup of coffee is fine — but what comes after is a distance too wide to close.

choices.text: Decline — 'Please don't worry about it. I'm really fine.'
choices.result_text:
{name} shakes the head and walks toward the subway.

Jiyeon doesn't follow. Instead, from behind:
'Why do you keep running away?'

{name} doesn't stop. But those words follow.
— Running? Is this running?
Jiyeon found herself more curious about {name} than ever.

choices.text: Accept — just the coffee. Once.
choices.result_text:
Sat across from her.
A café that felt expensive just sitting in it. ₩7,000 Americano.

'I wanted to hear about the gap on your résumé.'
She'd looked {name} up. Somehow.

{name} thought about how much to say.
This person — what did she actually want?

title: Her World
description:
Jiyeon said she was buying lunch. A promise.

She took {name} to a Korean restaurant in Cheongdam. Lunch set: ₩40,000.

{name} opened the menu, closed it, opened it again, closed it.

She pretended not to notice. Or really didn't.
After ordering she said:

'Actually I'm interested in investing. I'm studying for my father's company, but there's no one in my circle who does this, which is frustrating.'

{name} thought for a moment.
What exactly does this person want — impossible to read clearly.

choices.text: 'I'm studying it too. Let's talk.' — Approach as investment partners.
choices.result_text:
Two hours of real estate, pre-sales, investment talk.
Jiyeon knew a lot. Had studied hard.
What {name} knew and what she knew were different. Because of where they came from.
{name} tried to pay for the lunch. Reached — but she'd already put down the card.

choices.text: 'Let's just enjoy lunch today.' — Don't define the relationship yet.
choices.result_text:
Lunch was good. Conversation light.
On the way out she said: 'Where do you want to go next time?'
'Next time' was created. What kind of next time — still unknown.

title: After
description:
The morning after {name} told her everything —
Jiyeon sent a message first.

'I'm scared you might still be angry.
I talked so much yesterday... I'm a little weird, aren't I?'

{name} stared at the phone.

A woman with three layers of reason.
Because of her father's company. Because she needed an investor. And because she wanted someone close.

What can this become?

choices.text: 'You're not weird. That's just being human.' — Accept it.
choices.result_text:
Sent the reply.
A moment later, hers: 'You're weird too. That's why I like it.'
{name} half-smiled. Felt like there was one more reason to reach Gangnam.

choices.text: 'Jiyeon — Gangnam still comes first for me.' — Draw a clear line.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon went quiet, then: '...I understand. That's more honest.'
The next day, a document on pre-sale rights came from her.
'If you need help on this side, reach out. That part was genuine.'
Business partners — without the feelings.

choices.text: 'I understand all three reasons.' — No judgment.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon went quiet a moment, then said: '...That's the scariest thing you've said. Because I'm grateful.'
Gangnam and feelings and calculation all tangled in this.
Decided not to give up on it for being complicated.

title: Ten Years
description:
A KakaoTalk message.
'Hey {name}! It's me, Jaehyuk. Choi Jaehyuk from the army. You remember, right? I'm in Seoul — let's catch up.'

His profile photo: him standing in front of a foreign car.
Twenty-two, same barracks. Three years close, then lost touch after discharge.

Jaehyuk at the pojangmacha was different.
Good clothes, expensive watch, confident face.
'You haven't changed at all! Here, let me pour you one.'
He pays. No hesitation when the card comes out.

choices.text: Glad to see him — an old friend after a long time.
choices.result_text:
Old army stories stretched into the night.
First time laughing out loud in a while. A welcome face in a hard stretch.
'Let's meet up often, {name}. I'll be in touch.'
Jaehyuk seemed genuine. At least that night.

choices.text: Glad, but keeping some distance.
choices.result_text:
Clinked glasses and smiled — but something sat uneasily.
Someone who contacts you after ten years is doing this well.
Why now, why me.
{name} pushed that thought away. It's an old friend.

title: Brothers
description:
After that, Jaehyuk kept in touch.
Bought meals, bought drinks, sometimes tried to slip money over.

'You're struggling lately, aren't you? Take this, come on, we're not strangers.'
{name} didn't take it. But the gesture felt genuine.

Today: a café. Jaehyuk takes out his phone.
'{name}, honestly I've been making pretty good money investing. Pretty good money.'
Shows the screen. Profit graph. Numbers going sharply up.
'If you're interested I'll fill you in. No pressure.'

choices.text: Show interest — 'How does it work?'
choices.result_text:
Jaehyuk's eyes lit up.
'I knew you'd get it. I'll tell you everything slowly.'
The returns he showed were unrealistically good.
Too good to be good — {name} forgot that then.

choices.text: Thanks, but pass — 'Investing isn't really my thing.'
choices.result_text:
'Ah, I'm not saying do it now. Just saying.'
Jaehyuk laughed and changed subjects.
But that profit graph stayed in the mind.
If it's real... {name} shook the thought off. For now.

choices.text: Those returns are too good — quietly start to wonder.
choices.result_text:
'Jaehyuk — this looks too good. Is this actually real?'
Jaehyuk's expression froze for half a second, then cleared.
'Ha, that's exactly why everyone doubts it and passes. Your call.'
That half-second — {name} didn't miss it.

title: Last Chance
description:
Jaehyuk called with a serious tone. A hotel lounge.

'{name}, this is just between us.
Something big is coming in. Triple your principal. But there's only a slot until this week.'

He leans in.
'You want Gangnam, right. How long will you get there on a salary? This is the shortcut.
Trust me, yeah? Are we strangers? We lived and died together.'

The account balance comes to mind. Gangnam comes to mind.
And then Father comes to mind.

Decision. Now.

choices.text: Put in everything — trust Jaehyuk.
choices.result_text:
Cleaned out the account. Nearly everything.
Jaehyuk pats the shoulder. 'Good call. You'll be laughing soon.'

That night, {name} couldn't sleep.
Whether it was anticipation or dread — impossible to tell.

choices.text: Put in a portion — want in, but won't bet it all.
choices.result_text:
'Jaehyuk, this much is all I can do. More would be too much.'
Jaehyuk looks faintly disappointed. 'Well... still something. Thanks.'
Not going all-in was an instinct.
That instinct might save {name} later.

choices.text: Refuse. And quietly start looking into it.
choices.result_text:
'Let me think about it.' {name} left.
Went home and started searching.
The investment product Jaehyuk mentioned. The company name. Similar fraud cases.

Results started appearing one by one.
A cold feeling ran down the spine.

title: Gone
description:
Settlement day. Tried to reach Jaehyuk.

No 'Read' receipt.
Phone rings and rings, then drops.
KakaoTalk profile photo: gone.

Three days for unease to become certainty.

Searched the company name Jaehyuk had mentioned.
A victim support café comes up.
Decades of posts on the board. The same name. Choi Jaehyuk.

{name} wasn't alone.
'We lived and died together' —
the most expensive lie ever told.

choices.text: Fall apart — can't do anything for a while.
choices.result_text:
Spent days lying on the goshiwon floor.
Only looked at the ceiling. The account was empty. Gangnam felt farther.

But strangely — once you've hit the bottom, there's nowhere lower to go.
The only thing left to do was get back up.
Someday, without fail — take this money back.

choices.text: Join the victims' group — not alone in this.
choices.result_text:
Joined the café and posted.
'Me too. He was my army buddy.'

Comments: 'Same.' 'My classmate too.'
He always targeted people close. Used trust as his weapon.

Victims started gathering. {name} ended up at the center.
There was still a way to get some of it back.

title: Counter
description:
{name} spent a month quietly gathering.
Jaehyuk's investment product structure. Money flow. Testimony from other victims.

It was a textbook Ponzi scheme. New money covering old payouts.
Once the structure was understood, the weak points appeared.

Met Jaehyuk again. This time {name} called the meeting.
'Jaehyuk. I know everything. The company structure. The victims.'
Jaehyuk's face goes white.
'...What are you going to do.'

A moment of decision. What kind of person will {name} become?

choices.text: Turn him in — do the right thing.
choices.result_text:
Handed the evidence to the police. Along with victim statements.
Jaehyuk was arrested. {name} didn't get the money back.
But at least stopped more people from being hurt.

Im Sangchul said: 'Good. You protected something more important than money.'
{name} had empty hands — but could look in the mirror.

choices.text: Hold the leverage and negotiate — get my money back, and then some.
choices.result_text:
'I won't report you. But give me triple my money back. One week.'
Jaehyuk nodded, trembling. The money came.

One step closer to Gangnam. But that night,
{name} spent a long time thinking about how they were any different from Jaehyuk.
Couldn't find an answer.

choices.text: Pull him in and run a bigger scheme — turn fraud into business.
choices.result_text:
'Instead of reporting — let's work together. But this time, properly.'
In Jaehyuk's eyes: relief and fear mixed.

{name} crossed the line. Gangnam will get closer.
Fast. Dirty.
Is the apartment Dad never got — supposed to be bought with this money?
That question, {name} decided not to ask. For now.

title: Sangchul's Call
description:
A call from Im Sangchul after a long time.

'Minjun, I heard you've saved up some seed money. Something just came up.'

A villa right before redevelopment. The owner in a rush, listed well below market.
Sangchul had held it through his contacts.

'If the redevelopment is confirmed within a year, you're looking at double. If not — it sits.
Thirty years in this business, I think this one has decent odds.
But it's your call. I'm not recommending or warning.'

A significant portion of current funds. Not a gamble — but not safe either.

choices.text: Trust him — trust Sangchul's thirty years.
choices.result_text:
Stamped the contract with Sangchul.
He pats the shoulder. 'Good. Now waiting is the work.'
Real estate is different from stocks. Slower — but heavier.
Whatever happens, {name} got on the board for the first time.

choices.text: Put in only a little — don't get greedy.
choices.result_text:
'Not overextending is right.' Sangchul nods.
Half confidence, half bet.
{name} decided to stake only what fits in the bucket. That's how you last.

choices.text: Pass — protect the money for now.
choices.result_text:
'Good. The times you don't act are what keep you alive.'
Sangchul wasn't disappointed.
But a few months later, the redevelopment news came out.
Sangchul didn't mention it. {name} noticed on their own.

title: Make the Seed Money Work
description:
A text came from Sangchul.
"How've you been? You just crossed my mind."

I called him back. After a stretch of small talk, he said,
"Starting a new job at 33 and trying to pull together three billion won by 38... have you actually run the numbers?"

Minjun listened in silence.

"On a salary it's impossible. Even at a 30% savings rate in Seoul, you wouldn't clear a hundred million in five years.
You have to put the seed money to work. Stocks, real estate, a business — something.
What I'm saying is, you've got to learn something."

choices.text: "How should I start?" — ask in earnest
choices.result_text:
Sangchul thought for a long while before speaking.
"Start small at first. With money you can afford to lose and still learn from.
You lose some, and the market starts coming into focus."

After hanging up, {name} opened the investment tab for the first time.

choices.text: "Shouldn't saving come first?"
choices.result_text:
"Saving's the foundation, sure. But saving alone will never get you there."
Sangchul said it with a smile.
"Anyway, give it some thought. There's no rush."
The call ended. Something sat heavy in a corner of his chest.

choices.text: "I have my own way of doing things."
choices.result_text:
"Sure. You've got to figure it out for yourself in the end."
Sangchul laughed, unbothered.
{name} hung up and stared at the ceiling for a while.
What his own way actually was — he still wasn't sure.

title: The Presale Right
description:
Jiyeon called him aside, quietly.

"My father's company is putting up a presale development in Gangnam. It hasn't gone public yet.
If you just put down the deposit, the premium will be enormous. I'm only telling you."

{name} hesitated. This was an opportunity Jiyeon's world was offering him.
Take it, and he'd close in on Gangnam. But in that same moment, he'd be in her debt.
He'd be setting one foot inside her world.

"Why are you giving this to me?"
"...You really have to ask?" She smiled.

Money and feelings, both on the line.

choices.text: Take the chance — to get closer to Gangnam
choices.result_text:
He put down the deposit. He'd stepped one foot into Jiyeon's world.

She smiled, satisfied. "Good call."
But {name} knew. This wasn't free.
The closer Gangnam got, the closer she got too. Like a debt.

choices.text: Turn it down — I want to get there under my own power
choices.result_text:
"Thank you. But I want to do this on my own."
Jiyeon's expression hardened, subtly.
"...You really are a strange one. You're turning this down?"

She didn't understand. But {name} —
he liked the version of himself that owed her nothing.
Gangnam slipped further away, but he could hold his head up.

title: Easy Money
description:
The goshiwon, 2 a.m. Rent comes out of the account next week. One look at the balance and the first thing out of him is a sigh.

A text from an unknown number.
"Lend us just your bankbook and debit card — two million on the spot. You don't have to do anything.
One month, that's all. Zero risk. Contact us only if you're in a tight spot."

{name} knows what that is. A burner bank account — an account lent out so voice-phishing money can be laundered through it.
Someone else's stolen money would pass through his account.

Two million won. Four months of breathing room.
His finger hovers over the reply.

choices.text: Delete it — I won't sink that low
choices.result_text:
{name} blocked the number and flipped his phone face-down.
Two million won vanished before his eyes. The rent stayed right where it was.

A pathetic kind of pride, someone might sneer.
Still — he didn't want to live the way his father had, paying off that debt for six years.
He decided to go slow, with clean hands.
choices.foreshadow: Back then he thought it was the right call. What that choice would cost him later, he didn't yet know.

choices.text: Just this once. Lend out the account  (+2,000,000 won)
choices.result_text:
He sent his account number. An hour later, two million won landed.
So easy money like this really did exist in the world.

{name} stared at the figure for a long time. Along with the relief,
he felt something turn cold deep in his gut.
Whose tears this money had come from — he decided not to think about it.
choices.foreshadow: Once you've done it this way, you'll make the same choice the next time too. That's what a disposition is.

title: The Place It Passed Through

choices.text: Thank god. I go my own way
choices.result_text:
{name} let out a long breath.

Slow as it is, the honest road gets you furthest in the end.
Even if it's hard right now — he chose to believe that.

The rent was still unpaid. But his hands were clean.

description:
He was watching the news when a chyron scrolled past.

'Burner-account recruitment ring arrested — dozens of account holders charged. Up to 3 years in prison.'

That night, he deleted the text promising a two-million-won deposit.
He blocked the number.

He lay there a long while with the screen gone dark.
If he'd sent it back then — by now he'd be inside that very news chyron.

He'd have been dreaming of Gangnam with a criminal record.

title: The Price of the Account
description:
A phone call. A woman he didn't know was crying.
"I made a deposit from my account... they said it was a scam. They said it went to your account...
It's thirty million won. Please, please give it back..."

It was the account {name} had lent out.
Someone's entire savings had passed through it.

And the next day, another number.
"Hyungnim, you ran that clean. Get me a few more accounts and
I'll throw in another million per. You've already got your foot in anyway."

choices.text: Pull out right here — whatever it takes
choices.result_text:
{name} blocked every number, took the two million he'd received and added his own savings on top,
and sent back to the woman as much as he could manage. He closed the account too.

The balance was on the floor again. He didn't sleep for days.
But he pulled his foot out before he got dragged in deeper.
The chance to end it as a single mistake — was still there.

choices.text: It's already come to this, so go in deeper  (+3,000,000 won)
choices.result_text:
{name} blocked the woman's number. And the sound of her crying with it.
"I can get a few more."

It was a line already crossed. If going back wouldn't make him clean,
better to go all the way — that's how he talked himself into it.
The more money came in, the harder it got to look in the mirror.
Gangnam was getting closer. Built on someone else's hell.

title: The Second Coffee
description:
Out checking studio-apartment listings, he passed through that neighborhood and the light on at Sangchul's office caught his eye.

He wavered a moment over whether to go in, then pushed the door open.
Sangchul welcomed him. "You came. Want a coffee?"

He was unusually talkative today.
The story of coming up to Seoul from Chungcheong without a single connection.
The day he first set foot in Gangnam.

"Look at the people who made it into Gangnam. Every one of them had a connection somewhere.
Someone opened a door for them. The ones who knocked their way in alone — they're truly rare."

After a brief silence, Sangchul added,
"Once you've got a bit of seed money, there's a place I want to take you. A gathering that meets once a month.
Real estate, construction, capital. I can show you how Gangnam actually turns."

choices.text: "Anytime. Please, take me there."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul nodded.
"Alright. When you're ready, I'll be in touch.
There are things you need to see and learn in that room."

Walking out of the office, {name} thought:
some doors don't open by knocking.
Someone has to open them from the inside.

choices.text: "Thank you, but for now I want to try under my own power."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul looked at him for a moment. Then he smiled.
"Good. You need that confidence too.
But come find me when you hit a wall. The door's always open."

{name} chose to walk on his own two feet.
How long he could keep that up — that was still anyone's guess.

title: How Gangnam Turns
description:
Sangchul got in touch.
"That gathering's happening this month. Come with me."

A private room in a restaurant in the heart of Gangnam.
Business cards moved across every table, and big numbers were exchanged in soft voices.
Construction firms, developers, investment syndicates. Sangchul introduced him to each one.
"This one's a friend of mine. Someone I'm keeping an eye on."

In the middle of the conversation, one name slipped past, casually.
"What about Han PD Construction over there?" — someone said.
Sangchul changed the subject without a flicker in his expression.
{name} hung that name on a hook somewhere in his mind.

Off to one side of the room were people of a different air.
'Guaranteed returns,' 'short-term high yield.' Low voices, but familiar words.
Sangchul gave him a look. "Don't mix with that lot.
There's the real thing and the fake — telling them apart is the skill."

choices.text: Stick close to Sangchul and greet everyone
choices.result_text:
He took a card from everyone Sangchul introduced.
He could feel the weight of the information moving through this room.
Gangnam wasn't buildings — it was the web of these people.
{name} carefully set his foot on the outermost edge of that web.

choices.text: Drift toward the corner, toward the people talking guaranteed returns
choices.result_text:
Their words were sweet. Concrete figures, a plausible structure.
The longer {name} listened, the faster his heart beat.

On the way out, Sangchul said quietly,
"Those people — a lot of them get hauled in a few years later.
And the people around them go down with them."
{name} nodded. A little late.

title: The Casino Invitation
description:
A text came from Sangchul's number.

"What about this weekend? A few of us are heading to Jeongseon Casino.
I've booked a table room, so come on by, take it easy."

Jeongseon Casino. A place businesspeople go now and then.
Dress code. Chips. Strategy at the table.
Less like gambling than an admission ticket to a certain world.

{name} checked his account balance.

choices.text: "I'll come along" — follow him
choices.result_text:
On the bus to Jeongseon, Sangchul explained the basic rules of baccarat.
Banker and player. Martingale and the commission.
"Winning isn't the goal. The strategy is how little you lose."
To {name}, that sounded like it was about more than the game.

choices.text: "I don't think now's the time" — decline politely
choices.result_text:
Sangchul said, "Whenever you're ready."
It sounded like the offer stayed open.

title: Where Two Worlds Sit Side by Side
description:
With a decision looming, he went to see Sangchul.
To ask for advice.

In the course of the conversation, Jiyeon came up. He hadn't meant to, but
it came naturally — that he'd gotten to know her, that he'd been offered something on a real-estate deal.

Sangchul's expression changed.

"Jiyeon. Her surname's Han?" "Yes."
"Whose family is she from?" "Construction, I heard..."
Sangchul thought for a moment, then said, low,

"Han PD Construction."

That name. The very one that had slipped past at the last gathering.
Sangchul's face had gone rigid.
"She brought up a presale deal from that family, didn't she?"

choices.text: "Yes. Is there a problem?"
choices.result_text:
Sangchul chose his words, then brought them out slowly.
"There's some talk in the industry. Nothing certain — not yet.
But that presale — let me look into it."
"I'm not saying she's a bad person.
But the flow of money tied up in there — you need to understand it."

Walking out of the office, {name} thought:
the two worlds sat far closer together than he'd realized.

choices.text: "But you're in the same industry, Sangchul. You're competitors, so maybe..."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul showed a hurt look for a moment, then nodded.
"...That's possible. I could be wrong."
"But Minjun. Why would I lie to you?"

Those words followed him the whole way home.
{name} decided to push it down. For now.

title: A Call That Came Too Late
description:
A KakaoTalk came from Hyunsu.

"Hyung, do you happen to know Choi Jaehyuk?"

{name} set the phone down, then picked it up again.
"My army buddy. Why?"
"...Hyung, did you put money in with him?"

A brief silence.

"I joined an investment forum. I saw his name there.
Choi Jaehyuk. Victim warning. Suspected Ponzi structure. The posts go back a few months.
I didn't get tangled up in it myself... but you, hyung?"

choices.text: Call Jaehyuk right now and demand it back — maybe I can still pull it out
choices.result_text:
He made the call. Jaehyuk picked up — he could still be reached, for now.
"Hey, I think I need to pull my money out. Something urgent came up."
Jaehyuk went quiet for a beat, then said with a laugh,
"What are you talking about, man. You'll lose if you pull out now. Just a little longer and..."

With great difficulty, he salvaged only a part of it.
Where the rest had gone, there was no way to know.

Hyunsu said, "Hyung, I should've told you sooner. I'm sorry."
That hurt more. Because it wasn't Hyunsu's fault.

choices.text: "...It can't be Jaehyuk" — choose to trust his army friend
choices.result_text:
"Hyunsu, not everything in those forum posts is necessarily true.
Jaehyuk's a real friend of mine. We went through the army together, lived and died side by side."
Hyunsu was quiet for a moment, then said, "...Right. I guess I worried for nothing."

{name} set the phone down.
His heart beat a little faster.
Whether it was because he wanted to believe, or because he already knew — he couldn't tell.

choices.text: "I thought something was off too. Let's look into it together"
choices.result_text:
"Hyunsu, send me that forum link.
I'd been doing some digging myself, actually."
"You suspected it too, hyung?" "Yeah. But I wasn't sure."

The two of them started gathering information.
The pattern of relationships Jaehyuk had built, the flow of the money.
The picture grew sharper and sharper.
And the sharper it got, the more it made him sick.

title: The Things She Couldn't Say Back Then
description:
Jiyeon reached out first.
"Minjun, do you have time to meet for a bit?"

Across the café table, her face was different from usual.
The face of someone who'd been preparing for something a long time.

"I think I need to be honest with you."

She said her father's company was struggling.
That this presale had to go well.
That's why she needed investors, and why she'd pitched it to Minjun.
That part was true too.

"But that's not all of it.
My wish for you to do well — that was real too.
And... I was curious about you, and I wanted to be near you."

"All three are tangled together, and I don't know what kind of person I am.
Am I a bad person?"

choices.text: "Thank you for being honest. Let's figure out a way together."
choices.result_text:
Tears welled in Jiyeon's eyes.
"...Thank you. I'm not sure I deserve to hear that."

The two of them talked for a long time.
The real structure of the presale, the way out, the worst case.
This time with no calculation, nothing hidden.

Strangely — it felt more like a path toward Gangnam.
Not through money, but through a person.

choices.text: "You used me, didn't you." — lay the betrayal out plainly
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon lowered her head.
"You're right. You have every reason to feel that way."
She didn't argue.

Walking out of the café, {name} knew it hadn't lifted the weight off him.
He also knew she wasn't a bad person.
Which made it more complicated.

choices.text: "You lived in your world, and I made my own choice."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon looked at {name} for a long time.
"...There aren't many people who could say that."

{name} meant it.
His choices were his own.
Looking for someone to blame — that's the road that leads further from Gangnam.

She gave a small smile.
For the first time, an unguarded one.

title: The Things He Already Knew
description:
Jiyeon reached out first.
"Minjun, do you have time to meet for a bit?"

Sitting across from her at the café, {name} already remembered what Sangchul had said.
'That woman needs presale numbers — she's after your money.'

She opened her mouth.
The story of her father's company. The presale targets. And — why she'd pitched it to Minjun.

"But that's not all of it.
My wish for you to do well — that was real too.
And... I was curious about you, and I wanted to be near you."

"All three are tangled together, and I don't know what kind of person I am.
Am I a bad person?"

{name} already knew. Which made it stranger still — complication came before anger.

choices.text: "I knew. Even so, thank you for telling me yourself."
choices.result_text:
"...You knew?"
Jiyeon was lost for words for a moment.
"Then why are you still here?"
{name} answered by taking a sip of coffee instead.
That silence was the answer.

choices.text: "Thank you for telling me. But — what if you'd been honest from the start?"
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon lowered her head.
"...You're right. I should have said it from the beginning."
Honesty that came too late. Courage that came too late.
{name} had already known, but hearing it directly was another thing entirely.

choices.text: "That's just how people are. Your world had its own ways."
choices.result_text:
"You... already knew."
For the first time, Jiyeon's face had set down its defenses.
"And you can still say that?"
He'd thought a betrayal you saw coming would hurt less — it didn't, not quite.
Still, forgiveness was also a thing he did for himself.

title: The Rejection Email
description:
A mail notification popped up on his phone.

[Hiring Result] To Mr. Kim Minjun, applicant for the Management Support Team at Daehan Distribution Co., Ltd.

Hello. Thank you for your application.
After reviewing your submission, we regret to inform you that
we are unable to select you in this round of hiring.
We wish you the best in your future endeavors.

{name} closed the phone. Then he looked out the window for a while.

He consoled himself that it was the first rejection — but in truth it was the third.
When there's nothing to put on a résumé, you'd at least like a reason. They don't give that either.

choices.text: It's fine, look for the next posting
choices.result_text:
He opened the job app again. Similar postings, similar requirements, similar feel.
Hitting the apply button was a 0.3-second act of courage.
They usually reply about three weeks later — or never at all.

choices.text: Work on the résumé (revise the cover letter)
choices.result_text:
He opened the cover-letter file. He wrestled for an hour with how to fill the six-month gap.
It's not perfect, but it's better than before.
Every one of these lines will land in an interviewer's eyes someday.

title: The Goshiwon Owner's Meddling
description:
He ran into the goshiwon owner — the ajumma — in the hallway.

'Not heading out to work these days, are you, young man?'

It was phrased as a question, but it was a confirmed fact. There's nothing that happens in this building the ajumma doesn't know.

'There's a night shift open at the convenience store my nephew runs. It's not far either. You want it?'

It's no great position. But with his account in its current state, is this the time to be picky?

choices.text: Thank you. I'll start right away — convenience store night shift
choices.result_text:
He started the next day.
The wage is stingy, but now there's money coming in every month.
The gap between zero and one was bigger than he'd thought.
He bought the ajumma a case of drinks.

choices.text: I appreciate the thought. I'm looking for something better
choices.result_text:
The ajumma laughed, 'Sure, when you're young you should aim high.'
Back in his room, he opened the job postings again.
Choices carry responsibility. His account will show that responsibility.

title: What Came After
description:
He saw the name in the news.
Choi Jaehyuk.

Headline: "Pyramid investment fraud ring arrested, 2.3 billion won in damages."

{name} didn't open the article.
Because opening it felt like he already knew.

The choice from back then came to mind.
Whether he'd turned it over to the police, held leverage over him, or schemed the whole thing together —
that choice came back now, along with this news.

{name} looked out the window for a long time.

choices.text: Turning it over to the police was right — this news proves it  [take_high_road path]
choices.result_text:
The evidence {name} submitted contributed to this outcome.
Not getting his money back was still the case.
But an additional 2.3 billion won in damage was stopped.
Gangnam is still far off. Even so, he wasn't ashamed to look in the mirror.

choices.text: Back then I saved only myself — maybe that was the way to Gangnam  [crossed_line path]
choices.result_text:
He closed the article.
Whether what {name} had done stopped some of that 2.3 billion or added to it, there was no telling.
What kind of person he'd become on the road to Gangnam —
a day was coming when he could no longer dodge that question.

choices.text: Read it as a victim — so he got caught in the end after all  [jaehyuk_scammed path]
choices.result_text:
2.3 billion won. {name}'s money is in there somewhere too.
He won't get it all back. He won't know until the trial's over.
But strangely, closing the article, he could breathe a little easier.
That bastard got caught in the end. That's enough. For now.

title: Memory of the Starting Line
description:
Gangnam had drawn close.

Through all this walking, {name} had either kept someone at his side — or failed to.

He thought of Daeun.
That hand sliding a coffee across the convenience-store counter.
The words she'd said: "You did well today too."

Where she'd be on the day he reached Gangnam — {name} couldn't know.
But just remembering that beginning
seemed to make the reason he'd come this far come clear.

choices.text: Daeun is at the end of this road — to reach Gangnam together  [daeun_together_path]
choices.result_text:
He sent Daeun a single text.
"Almost there. Just like we promised."
A reply came. "I'm waiting too."

{name} slipped the phone into his pocket and started walking again.
This was the last stretch now.

choices.text: Because I let her go, I made it this far  [daeun_let_her_go]
choices.result_text:
Daeun is living well back home.
And {name} is one step short of Gangnam.

The two of them had chosen different directions,
but both seemed to have drawn closer to happiness, each in their own way.
{name} thought that was enough. For now.

title: Redevelopment Confirmed
description:
A call came from Sangchul.

"Minjun. It's confirmed."

The official notice designating the redevelopment district. {name} checked the figure twice.
The market price had jumped more than two and a half times.

Sangchul said it briefly.
"This is real estate. Slow, but certain."

For the first time, he felt he'd won at the real table.

choices.text: Ask him to let me know if there's another chance
choices.result_text:
"Of course. My network in this game is everything."
Sangchul laughed and hung up.
{name} gazed out the window for a moment.
Seoul looked a little different. Not Gangnam yet, but.

choices.text: Use these gains as fuel for the next bet
choices.result_text:
When you win, you have to bet bigger.
{name} was already calculating the next opportunity.
A structure where money brings in money. He was starting to see it.

title: Redevelopment Falls Through
description:
A call came from Sangchul.

"...Minjun. I'm sorry."

The redevelopment-district designation was pushed to the next session.
Effectively dead. The money he got back had the losses already subtracted.

He said nothing more.
He didn't say it was the first time in thirty years in this game that he'd been wrong.
Just that he was sorry.

choices.text: It can't be helped — I knew the risk going in
choices.result_text:
"Thanks, Sangchul. I made the call myself."
{name} said it. It was sincere, partly,
and partly because he had to frame it that way to move forward.
The money lost is tuition. Steep tuition, at that.

choices.text: Honestly, it feels like a betrayal
choices.result_text:
After hanging up, he couldn't do anything for a while.
The injustice of it ran deeper than the anger. Because he'd trusted him.
Sangchul might be blameless.
But right now, that was no comfort.

title: The Premium
description:
A text came from Jiyeon.

One emoticon. And a number.

{name} stared at the screen for a moment.
As if to confirm it was real.

He'd stepped into her world,
and this time, his side had won.

But strangely, it felt like he'd repaid a debt to her.

choices.text: Thank Jiyeon
choices.result_text:
"This is thanks to you. I mean it."
Jiyeon was silent a moment, then replied.
"...That's what I wanted to hear."
One step closer to Gangnam. With her.

choices.text: Now I stand equal to her world
choices.result_text:
Gratitude only takes a moment.
{name} was already linking these gains to the next plan.
Not Jiyeon's world, but his own.
That, he thought, was the real entry into Gangnam.

title: Pre-Sale Cancelled
description:
A text arrived saying the pre-sale had been cancelled.

Jiyeon called directly.
"I'm sorry. I didn't know either."

There was something genuine in her voice. Maybe.

The deposit was gone.
Jiyeon's world didn't always win.

{name} stared at the ceiling. For a long time.

choices.text: "It's okay — not your fault"
choices.result_text:
"It's fine." The words came out easy enough.
Honestly, it wasn't fine.
But {name} didn't want to fall apart in front of her.
Gangnam felt further away. But the pride held.

choices.text: "Trusting Jiyeon was a mistake"
choices.result_text:
"I shouldn't have trusted you."
Said it. Hung up.
Maybe Jiyeon's world had only ever looked glamorous from the outside.
{name} saw her differently now.

title: The Call
description:
Every Sunday evening. Called Dad.
A habit kept since high school.

The line rang. Once. Twice. Three times. Four.
Dad picked up.
"...Yeah."

That was how it started. {name} had nothing to say either.
Six years ago — after the call about the debt from a bad loan guarantee,
Dad stopped reaching out first.
Shamefaced, maybe. Sorry, maybe. Both, maybe.

The factory layoff. The apartment lost.
Neither of them brought those up. But both knew.

"Did you... eat?"
Dad's first words.

choices.text: "Yeah. You too?"
choices.result_text:
"Ate."

A long silence. {name} hung up first.
Spent thirty seconds after the call trying to think of what to say.

Why nothing ever comes out during the call.
Maybe because just hearing the voice already says everything.

choices.text: "Yeah. Dad, I think things are going to work out."
choices.result_text:
"...Yeah?"
Dad's voice shifted slightly. In that one short word.

After hanging up, {name} thought:
There's still so much left to show him. And time isn't endless.

choices.text: Just ask how he is and hang up quickly
choices.result_text:
Call duration: 23 seconds.
"How are you." "Fine." "Okay, hang up then."

{name} put the phone down and stared at the ceiling.
Too many things that couldn't fit into 23 seconds.

title: One Message
description:
A KakaoTalk from an unknown number.

"Minjun? This is Mrs. Choi, the neighbor from Changwon.
I got your number from your father.
He seems to be going to the hospital these days.
Not sure if it's serious, but I thought I should let his son know."

{name} read the screen twice.
Called Dad. The line rang. No answer.
Five minutes later a text came.
"I'm fine, don't worry about it."

choices.text: Reply that you'll come down next week
choices.result_text:
Dad didn't reply.
That wasn't a no, and {name} knew it.
Searched for train tickets. KTX Changwon-Jungang, two and a half hours.
Some things come before money — learned that this time.

choices.text: Call to check — can't be that serious
choices.result_text:
Called again. He answered this time.
"I'm fine. Just a regular check-up. Nothing major."
Firm. {name} didn't press further.
Wanted to believe he was fine.
The difference between believing and wanting to believe — couldn't tell them apart yet.

choices.text: Can't afford to go down right now — once things settle
choices.result_text:
Pulled up train tickets. Then closed the tab.
Not yet. A little more money first, then go down.
Just a little more.

How much was "a little" — {name} didn't really know.

title: Mom's Call
description:
Mom called. She hadn't been in touch in a long time.

"Minjun."

Just the voice was enough to know.

Dad had collapsed. A cerebrovascular episode. Changwon Sungsim Hospital ER.
Stabilized now. Conscious, talking.

"Should only need a few days in hospital. No surgery.
But going forward he has to be careful.
The doctor said... if he doesn't manage it properly, it could happen again anytime."

{name}'s hands trembled briefly.

choices.text: Go down right now
choices.result_text:
Booked the first KTX to Changwon. 5 a.m. from Seoul Station.
On the train, tried to picture Dad's face.
Started calculating when the last time was —
Stopped. Too long ago.

choices.text: Say you'll go down within the week
choices.result_text:
"I'll come on the weekend."
Mom went quiet for a moment.
"Yeah. I called because I thought your dad would worry a lot."
Something buried under those words.
{name} hung up, then thought about how far away the weekend felt.

choices.text: Send money — too busy with things here
choices.result_text:
Transferred the money. For hospital expenses.
Mom said "Thank you."
Dad would ask whose money it was.
{name} decided not to think about what Mom would say.

title: Changwon
description:
Changwon Sungsim Hospital. Room 301.

The hallway smelled of disinfectant. Different air from Seoul.
Asked the nurse for Dad's room number.

Opened the door.
Dad was sitting up in bed, looking out the window.
Changwon sky. Low buildings. Factory smokestacks.

Thin hands. Hands that had gripped factory floors his whole life.
Shoulders more hunched. Hair more white.

{name} paused at the doorway.
Dad turned around without a sound. Eyes met.

A long silence passed.

Dad spoke. "...Minjun."
Then another pause.
"I'm sorry."

choices.text: "It's not your fault, Dad." — first time saying those words
choices.result_text:
Six years of unsaid words.

Dad's eyes reddened. He took {name}'s hand.
The hands hardened from factory work. They were trembling.

Neither of them spoke for a long time.
It was enough. That silence felt comfortable for the first time.

On the KTX back to Seoul, {name} watched out the window for a long time.

choices.text: "When I make it to Gangnam, you're the first person I'll bring."
choices.result_text:
Dad smiled faintly.
"...Okay. I believe you."

Factory smokestacks through the window. Where Dad spent his whole life.
{name} made a silent promise. No matter what.

choices.text: Can't say anything — just sit beside him
choices.result_text:
There was so much to say, and none of it came out.
Just sat down beside him. Dad didn't speak either.

Two hours like that.
Later, {name} would understand that was the best way.

title: After That
description:
After coming back from Changwon, the calls with Dad changed.

Still not many words.
But now there was something more after "did you eat."

Today Dad called first.
Not Sunday evening. Wednesday afternoon.

"Minjun. How's the weather in Seoul?"

choices.text: "Cold here. Cold there too, right?" — just talk about small things
choices.result_text:
Fifteen minutes of weather, the neighborhood, nothing in particular.

After hanging up, {name} was smiling.

Not a word about Gangnam.
But today that felt better. Because Dad called first.

choices.text: "I'm doing well lately, Dad. Don't worry."
choices.result_text:
Dad's voice sounded warm.

"I'm doing fine too. And so are you."
A brief silence.
"...Yeah. Me too."

That was all. But the feeling after the call was different today.

title: Hey, Actually Me Too...
description:
The second meeting at the pojangmacha went late.

Jaehyuk poured another round of soju.
His eyes were hazier than usual.

"Hey {name}. I... actually, I got burned too, back then."

{name} put down the chopsticks.

"A senior I knew talked to me about an investment. Said it was a great opportunity. You know how rough things were for me at the time. So I put money in. And then..."

Jaehyuk trails off.

"The strange thing is, later that senior asked if I wanted to become one of the operators. Said I'd be good at it. Looking back, it's funny."

He laughs bitterly.

Seems like he's about to say more — takes a sip instead. That's all for tonight.

choices.text: "So what happened?" — listen comfortably
choices.result_text:
Jaehyuk laughed. 'Ah, that's ancient history. Things are fine now, right?'
He changed the subject. {name} didn't push.
But those words kept nagging. So what happened, exactly.

choices.text: "Being an operator... you still doing that now?" — ask directly
choices.result_text:
Jaehyuk's eyes hardened for a moment.
'...What are you talking about. That's all in the past.'
He smiled and offered more to drink.
{name} accepted the glass, and didn't forget that brief flash in his eyes.

title: No-Strings Help
description:
Met at a cafe. Jaehyuk said he had good news.

It wasn't about investments.

"Hey, I know this guy who's an HR team leader at a mid-size company — send him your resume. I already mentioned you."

{name} paused.

"Why are you doing this for me?"

Jaehyuk smiled. "Come on, what are we to each other? You think I forgot how good you were to me in the army? I haven't."

He held out a business card with a contact on it.

Needs thinking through. Is this genuine goodwill — or a way to pull {name} in deeper?

choices.text: "Thanks. You're a real friend." — accept the offer
choices.result_text:
Took the card. Plan to reach out.
Jaehyuk really did have a good side.
What {name} didn't know then — that would make what came later hurt more.

choices.text: "Jaehyuk, honestly — why are you so good to me?" — probe the motive
choices.result_text:
A flash of hurt crossed Jaehyuk's face.
'...You think I'm doing this for something? That hurts.'
{name} hovered somewhere between guilt and suspicion.
Took the card. Never called.

title: Back from Zero
description:
A month since getting scammed.

Sat and calculated the amount lost.
Calculated it again. The number didn't change.

{name} took out a notebook.

What was in the account when first coming to this city?
Almost nothing, back then too. And somehow it worked out.

The difference between now and then —
Meeting someone like Choi Jaehyuk.
And now knowing why those words sounded so sweet.

{name} started writing.

choices.text: Write down what was learned, not what was lost — turn this into money
choices.result_text:
Wrote down everything Jaehyuk had said.
How he'd played on emotions. Which words had made the heart waver.
This was expensive tuition. But if tuition was paid, something had to be learned.
{name} closed the notebook and turned the computer back on.

choices.text: Get up early tomorrow morning — start over from the basics
choices.result_text:
Set the alarm for 6 a.m.
No grand plan. Just: get up in the morning, eat, do something.
That was all. That was where it started.
Thought of Jaehyuk for a moment — then opened the notebook.

title: Thin Wall
description:
3 a.m. Can't sleep.

A sound from the next room. At first thought it was a TV — no. Someone crying. Muffled. Through a single sheet of plasterboard.

Everyone here is getting through the night for their own reasons.

choices.text: Put in earplugs — not my business
choices.result_text: The sound disappeared. Or rather, became inaudible. Something inside went quiet too. Whether that's self-protection or just going numb — couldn't tell.

choices.text: Knock once on the wall — asking if they're okay
choices.result_text:
The sound stopped. A brief silence. Then a low, small voice. "Yes."

That was enough. A conversation through a wall, with someone whose name and face are unknown.

choices.text: Stare at the ceiling too — get through the night together
choices.result_text: How many people here are sleeping comfortably? That thought felt strangely comforting. Not alone — in the strangest possible way.

title: First Day on the App
description:
Desk in the gosiwon. Opened a stock brokerage account for the first time.

Charts going up and down. Red, blue. All of it is someone's money. And from now on, {name}'s money goes in here too.

Not scared — more like: this is real now.

choices.text: Put in ₩10,000 — have to feel it to understand it
choices.result_text:
₩10,000. A small number — but now this chart is {name}'s.
Up feels good, down feels scary. That's what to learn first.

choices.text: Read a book first — understand it before going in
choices.result_text:
Account created. No money in yet.
Better to know what it is before jumping in.

title: First Line of the Cover Letter
description:
Laptop screen. Cover letter question 1.

"Please describe your motivation for applying."

The cursor has been blinking for a minute. Age 33. No work history. Three-year gap. How does this get written? Honest means rejected; polished means it doesn't sound like me.

choices.text: Write honestly — explain the gap
choices.result_text:
Wrote it. The reason for the three years. Reading it back, it looks bleak.
But it's me. Starting from here.

choices.text: Dress it up — make it sound good
choices.result_text:
Came out polished. It's all true, but not all of it.
If the interview asks about this, it has to hold up. That's part of the prep too.

choices.text: Just submit — speed over perfection
choices.result_text:
Sent.
Doesn't have to be perfect. Submitting is better than not.

title: Idea Notebook
description:
Gosiwon bed. Smartphone notes app.

Thoughts that had been in {name}'s head since before coming to Seoul. Writing them out now, they look small. But if not written down, they'll disappear.

Stuck on the very first line.

choices.text: Search it right now — see if it already exists
choices.result_text:
Something similar already existed. Felt disappointed — then: I can do it better.
Execution beats first-mover advantage.

choices.text: Just write everything down — judge later
choices.result_text:
Fourteen ideas. Some ridiculous, some might be something.
Not sorting them yet. Ideas need volume first.

title: First Meetup
description:
Cafe. First meeting of a finance study group found online.

Everyone had jobs. {name} didn't. Got handed business cards. Had nothing to hand back — just saved their numbers.

Walking home, a strange feeling. Is this what networking is?

choices.text: Saved their contacts — might be useful later
choices.result_text: Saved. Names, jobs, interests. One-sided for now — but relationships are made by whoever remembers first.

choices.text: Felt uneasy walking home — what was I trying to get here?
choices.result_text:
They call it networking — but gathering without purpose is just acquaintances.
Next time, decide what to give and what to get before going.

title: Three Hours of Charts
description:
Gosiwon room. 2 a.m.

Technical indicators, moving averages, trading volume. Watched three YouTube lectures. Starting to see something, maybe — or maybe not yet.

2 a.m.

choices.text: Keep watching — something's about to click
choices.result_text:
4 a.m. Eyes aching.
But now MACD makes sense. Can feel understanding accumulating.

choices.text: Sleep — fresh mind tomorrow
choices.result_text:
Closed the laptop.
Studying needs to be consistent. One hour tomorrow beats pulling an all-nighter tonight.

title: Account Balance
description:
A month passed.

Opened the mobile banking app. Gosiwon rent, phone bill, transport, food. Transaction after transaction draining out.

Balance: {money}.

Knew it mentally — but seeing it in numbers was different.

choices.text: Listed out expenses — where can I cut?
choices.result_text: Broke it down by category. The only thing cuttable was food. Convenience store lunch box, ₩2,800. Two meals a day: ₩160,000 a month. Knowing the numbers made it less frightening somehow.

choices.text: Closed the app — check it later
choices.result_text: If you don't look it doesn't exist. Knew that wasn't true. The screen went dark, and {name}'s reflection looked back.

choices.text: Looked for part-time work right away
choices.result_text: Opened the job app. Convenience store, warehouse, gas station. ₩9,860/hr. Eight hours a day: ₩2.1M a month. Do it or not — decided to think again tomorrow.

title: Little by Little
description:
A month passed.

Opened the mobile banking app. Things went out, yes — but for the first time, more came in.

Balance: {money}.

Not a big number. Not something to brag about. But {name} stared at the screen for a while. First time the account had grown instead of shrunk.

choices.text: Took a screenshot — keeping a record
choices.result_text: Saved to the photo album. When this number looks laughably small someday, will look back at it then. Keeping the starting point.

choices.text: Wrote down next month's goal
choices.result_text: Opened a notes app. Next month's target balance. Wrote one number. What had been vague had a concrete box for the first time.

choices.text: Thought: this is nothing — still so far
choices.result_text: 0.0-something percent of ₩3 billion. Can't get comfortable with this. {name} closed the app. Satisfaction was a luxury — not yet.

title: This Is Actually Working
description:
A month passed.

Opened the mobile banking app. And looked again.

Balance: {money}.

A month ago it was ₩500,000. {name} traced the number with a finger. Counted the digits three times. Correct.

Scared. Happy, but scared. Because it's unclear if this is skill or luck.

choices.text: This is luck — don't get carried away
choices.result_text: Know that getting excited is when you lose. Mistaking one lucky break for skill is dangerous next time. {name} stayed calm and thought through the next move.

choices.text: Have to go bigger — this is the moment
choices.result_text: Not riding this momentum would be stupid. {name}'s pulse quickened. More, bigger. The thought wouldn't leave. Whether that was a good sign or bad — unknown yet.

choices.text: Decided not to tell anyone
choices.result_text: The moment you talk about money it gets complicated. Family, friends — not yet. {name} put the phone face down. A secret only {name} knows.
